title: Adaptive region-tier prioritization for canary version pinning with weighted graceful fallbacks
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Current rollout logic treats region selection, customer tier, and model variant fallback as mostly independent heuristics. That causes user-visible flapping for stateful sessions: users pinned to a canary variant in one region can be abruptly routed to a cheaper quantized variant in another tier during capacity pressure, breaking latency and quality invariants. We need a cohesive policy that: (1) preserves session affinity during progressive (canary/A-B) rollouts; (2) respects customer tier (paid vs free) to favour higher-quality variants without manual overrides; (3) exposes a deterministic, auditable fallback weight model for graceful degradation to cheaper variants and regions when capacity is constrained. This ticket defines the design, acceptance criteria, and implementation plan for an "adaptive region-tier prioritization" router which combines weighted fallback, session-aware pin TTLs, and canary percentage evolution with rollback triggers.
acceptance_criteria: Router evaluates region + tier + model-variant score and produces deterministic route decisions for identical request metadata (region, tier, session_id, version pin)
Session affinity TTL supports adaptive decay: short TTL for low-entropy sessions, extended TTL if user receives >80% responses from pinned variant over 15m window
Canary rollout controller exposes percentage and time-based ramp with automatic rollback when quality metrics breach thresholds

Fallbacks are weighted and logged: when primary variant is unavailable, router chooses fallback probabilistically according to configured weights and records the chosen variant and reason in audit logs
Unit and integration tests cover tie-breakers between region preference and tier preference (e.g., paid user in remote region vs free user in local region)
Performance: route resolution adds <1ms p50 CPU time in hot path and no measurable impact on tail latency (p99 token latency unchanged within 2%)
Monitoring: dashboards for route decisions, fallback rates, canary success metrics, and customer-impacting fallback exposures are present and linked in the PR
implementation_notes: High-level approach: 1) Introduce composite scoring: score = alpha*region_affinity + beta*tier_priority + gamma*variant_quality_score + delta*session_pin_bonus. Coefficients are cluster-configurable. 2) Session pin TTL becomes adaptive TTL that increments when variance from pinned variant is low and decrements when we observe fallbacks. 3) Implement a weighted-fallback engine: fallback manifests list candidate variants/regions with weight and compatibility tags. Router samples deterministically using request-hash+epoch to make fallback reproducible during an epoch. 4) Canary controller orchestrates ramp: initial tie-breaker gives strict version-affinity for percent X of sessions; ramp uses cohort-based sticky allocation to reduce cross-session thrash. 5) Add audit metadata to trace headers and event logs for downstream analysis. Tradeoffs: extra scoring step increases CPU; deterministic sampling reduces randomness but may bias some user cohorts if hashing distribution is skewed. Mitigations: expose coeffs and epoch seed as config and rotate seed on major rollouts. Edge cases: stateful streaming sessions require immediate affinity; for long-lived streams we will pin until explicit session close or TTL expiry.
rollout_plan: Week 1: Feature-flagged deploy of scoring logic and adaptive TTL in staging; run canary with internal traffic only
Week 2: 1% external traffic with rollout controller + observability; collect quality and latency metrics
Week 3: 10% traffic and expanded region coverage; adjust alpha/beta/gamma based on SLO impact
Week 4: 50% traffic with gradual TTL extension for cohorts that are stable; enable weighted fallback manifests for non-critical tiers
Rollback: Immediate full rollback if canary quality delta > 2% or error rate spike > 3x baseline for 10 minutes
